note: Teacher-curated first-pass lesson blueprints for NCERT-aligned Grade 6 learning. Mathematics chapter names and first-pass subtopics are mapped to the official NCERT Ganita Prakash Grade 6 Reprint 2026-27 book; chapter-level review remains required. Science is an initial concept map and must be checked against the official Curiosity textbook before being marked complete. The official textbook remains hosted by NCERT; these blueprints do not include textbook text.

steps.title: Notice the endpoints
steps.text: A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one starting point. A line has no endpoints.

steps.title: Compare the drawings
steps.text: Follow each drawing: the segment stops at both ends, the ray continues in one direction, and the line continues in both directions.

steps.title: Explain the difference
steps.text: Choose the drawing that has two endpoints and tell how you know.

challenge.question: Which drawing has exactly one endpoint?

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Measure an angle
lessons.caption: Rotate a ray around a fixed vertex and estimate the opening before reading its measure.

steps.title: Find the vertex
steps.text: The two arms meet at the vertex. Keep the vertex fixed while the ray turns.

steps.title: Estimate the opening
steps.text: Compare the opening with a right angle to make a first estimate.

steps.title: Measure carefully
steps.text: Align a protractor's centre with the vertex and its zero line with one arm, then read where the other arm crosses the scale.

challenge.question: What should stay fixed while you rotate the ray?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

steps.text: Acute is less than 90 degrees; obtuse is between 90 and 180 degrees; straight is 180 degrees.

steps.title: Classify it

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Angle
lessons.caption: Two rays with the same endpoint form an angle. The shared endpoint is the vertex; the rays are its arms.

steps.title: Find the vertex
steps.text: The common endpoint of the two rays is called the vertex.

steps.title: Find the arms
steps.text: The two rays starting at the vertex are the arms of the angle.

steps.title: Explore the opening
steps.text: Rotate one arm and watch the opening change while the vertex stays fixed.

challenge.question: What do we call the common endpoint of the two arms?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Comparing Angles
lessons.caption: Compare the opening between the arms. Angle size depends on the opening, not on how long the arms are drawn.

steps.title: Look at the opening
steps.text: An angle with a wider opening is larger than one with a narrower opening.

steps.title: Change arm length
steps.text: Make an arm longer without rotating it. The angle's opening stays the same, so its measure does not change.

steps.title: Compare and explain
steps.text: Choose the wider opening and explain why arm length alone does not decide angle size.

challenge.question: If an arm gets longer but does not rotate, does the angle change?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Making Rotating Arms
lessons.caption: Keep the vertex fixed and rotate one arm. Predict whether the opening becomes wider or narrower before you move it.

steps.title: Start with two arms
steps.text: The arms meet at a fixed vertex to form an angle.

steps.title: Predict and rotate
steps.text: Predict what will happen, then rotate one arm and observe the opening.

steps.title: Describe the change
steps.text: Explain how turning an arm changes the angle while the vertex remains in place.

challenge.question: When you rotate one arm farther away from the other, what happens to the opening?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Special Types of Angles
lessons.caption: Change the angle opening and identify it using the chapter's angle categories.

steps.title: Estimate the opening
steps.text: Compare the angle with a square corner, which is a right angle of 90 degrees.

steps.title: Sort the angle
steps.text: An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees; an obtuse angle is greater than 90 but smaller than 180 degrees; a straight angle is 180 degrees.

steps.title: Explain your choice
steps.text: Name the angle type and use its opening or measure as evidence.

challenge.question: What type of angle measures exactly 90 degrees?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Measuring Angles
lessons.caption: Estimate the opening first. When using a protractor, place its centre on the vertex and align the baseline with one arm.

steps.title: Estimate first
steps.text: Compare the opening with a right angle to estimate whether it is less than, equal to, or greater than 90 degrees.

steps.title: Align the protractor
steps.text: Put the protractor's centre on the vertex and align one arm with the zero line.

steps.title: Read the measure
steps.text: Read the scale where the second arm crosses it. Check that you used the scale starting at zero on the aligned arm.

challenge.question: Where should the centre of the protractor be placed?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Drawing Angles
lessons.caption: Draw a target angle by marking the vertex, aligning a protractor with the first arm, marking the target measure, and drawing the second arm.

steps.title: Mark the vertex
steps.text: Place a point for the vertex and draw the first arm.

steps.title: Mark the measure
steps.text: Align the protractor's centre with the vertex and its zero line with the first arm. Mark the required angle.

steps.title: Draw and check
steps.text: Draw the second arm through the mark, then check the angle's opening and measure.

challenge.question: What must align with the protractor's zero line?
challenge.success_feedback: Good thinking! Explain the clue that helped you decide.

lessons.subject: Mathematics

lessons.title: Types of Angles and their Measures

steps.title: Match type and measure
steps.text: Acute angles are below 90 degrees; right angles are 90 degrees; obtuse angles are between 90 and 180 degrees; straight angles are 180 degrees.

steps.title: Read or estimate
steps.text: Use a right angle as a reference, or measure with a correctly aligned protractor.

steps.title: Justify the type
